blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 2.8
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 2.8

blocks.text: शरीरं हविः
blocks.directed: [slowly] शरीरं हविः

blocks.text: Śarīraṃ haviḥ.
blocks.directed: Śarīraṃ haviḥ.

blocks.text: The body is the sacrificial offering.
blocks.directed: The body is the sacrificial offering.

blocks.text: Congratulations, You’re the Sacrifice.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, You’re the Sacrifice.

blocks.text: RIGHT.
blocks.directed: RIGHT.

blocks.text: Before anybody gets any ideas, let’s establish something important.
blocks.directed: Before anybody gets any ideas, let’s establish something important.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja is not telling practitioners to physically burn themselves.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja is not telling practitioners to physically burn themselves.

blocks.text: The fire in question is the supreme fire of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The fire in question is the supreme fire of consciousness.

blocks.text: And the body is offered through the dissolution of identification with it as the ultimate Self.
blocks.directed: And the body is offered through the dissolution of identification with it as the ultimate Self.

blocks.text: Now let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Now let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Śarīra — body.
blocks.directed: Śarīra — body.

blocks.text: Havis — sacrificial oblation or offering; haviḥ is its nominative form.
blocks.directed: Havis — sacrificial oblation or offering; haviḥ is its nominative form.

blocks.text: And this refers us to the ancient Indian sacrificial vocabulary of yajña.
blocks.directed: And this refers us to the ancient Indian sacrificial vocabulary of yajña.

blocks.text: The fire.
blocks.directed: The fire.

blocks.text: The offering.
blocks.directed: The offering.

blocks.text: The act of offering.
blocks.directed: The act of offering.

blocks.text: The officiant.
blocks.directed: The officiant.

blocks.text: The divine recipient.
blocks.directed: The divine recipient.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, these are differentiated elements of a ritual.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, these are differentiated elements of a ritual.

blocks.text: Somebody performs the sacrifice.
blocks.directed: Somebody performs the sacrifice.

blocks.text: Something is offered.
blocks.directed: Something is offered.

blocks.text: The offering goes into the fire.
blocks.directed: The offering goes into the fire.

blocks.text: The ritual is directed towards a divine reality.
blocks.directed: The ritual is directed towards a divine reality.

blocks.text: But Trika makes an extraordinary internal transformation of this structure.
blocks.directed: But Trika makes an extraordinary internal transformation of this structure.

blocks.text: The body becomes the offering.
blocks.directed: The body becomes the offering.

blocks.text: Consciousness becomes the fire.
blocks.directed: Consciousness becomes the fire.

blocks.text: And the false identification of the limited body as the ultimate perceiver is consumed.
blocks.directed: And the false identification of the limited body as the ultimate perceiver is consumed.

blocks.text: Now, notice the specificity.
blocks.directed: Now, notice the specificity.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja isn’t merely saying:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Kṣemarāja isn’t merely saying:

blocks.text: “Stop being attached to your body.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Stop being attached to your body.”

blocks.text: He’s talking about the pramātṛ, the knowing subject.
blocks.directed: He’s talking about the pramātṛ, the knowing subject.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, you identify the knower with your embodied individuality.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, you identify the knower with your embodied individuality.

blocks.text: “I am this body.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am this body.”

blocks.text: “My eyes are seeing.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “My eyes are seeing.”

blocks.text: “My brain is thinking.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “My brain is thinking.”

blocks.text: “My personal history defines what I am.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “My personal history defines what I am.”

blocks.text: But remember the very first sūtra.
blocks.directed: But remember the very first sūtra.

blocks.text: Caitanyam ātmā.
blocks.directed: Caitanyam ātmā.

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: From the standpoint of Kṣemarāja’s nondual metaphysics, the body itself belongs to the field of manifestation.
blocks.directed: From the standpoint of Kṣemarāja’s nondual metaphysics, the body itself belongs to the field of manifestation.

blocks.text: It is not the ultimate foundation of the conscious subject.
blocks.directed: It is not the ultimate foundation of the conscious subject.

blocks.text: So what does it mean to offer the body?
blocks.directed: So what does it mean to offer the body?

blocks.text: It means that the body, together with its subtle forms and the structures of limited identification, is recognised as an expression within supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: It means that the body, together with its subtle forms and the structures of limited identification, is recognised as an expression within supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: The body is not destroyed.
blocks.directed: The body is not destroyed.

blocks.text: Its erroneous status as an independently existing ultimate Self is relinquished.
blocks.directed: Its erroneous status as an independently existing ultimate Self is relinquished.

blocks.text: Imagine standing before a fire.
blocks.directed: Imagine standing before a fire.

blocks.text: You take the entire notion:
blocks.directed: [short pause] You take the entire notion:

blocks.text: “I am nothing more than this limited organism.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am nothing more than this limited organism.”

blocks.text: And you offer it into the recognition:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And you offer it into the recognition:

blocks.text: “My deepest nature is the consciousness in which this organism, its experiences, and the universe itself are manifest.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “My deepest nature is the consciousness in which this organism, its experiences, and the universe itself are manifest.”

blocks.text: The body hasn’t vanished.
blocks.directed: The body hasn’t vanished.

blocks.text: You’ve not stopped eating.
blocks.directed: You’ve not stopped eating.

blocks.text: You’ve not magically become impervious to a falling coconut.
blocks.directed: You’ve not magically become impervious to a falling coconut.

blocks.text: But its ontological status within your understanding has changed.
blocks.directed: But its ontological status within your understanding has changed.

blocks.text: And the beauty is that Kṣemarāja draws on the Vijñānabhairava to explain this inner sacrifice.
blocks.directed: And the beauty is that Kṣemarāja draws on the Vijñānabhairava to explain this inner sacrifice.

blocks.text: He describes the elements, senses, their objects, and mind as offerings into the fire of consciousness.
blocks.directed: He describes the elements, senses, their objects, and mind as offerings into the fire of consciousness.

blocks.text: And the power that performs the offering is itself cetanā, conscious Śakti.
blocks.directed: And the power that performs the offering is itself cetanā, conscious Śakti.

blocks.text: So who’s the priest?
blocks.directed: So who’s the priest?

blocks.text: Śakti.
blocks.directed: Śakti.

blocks.text: What’s the offering?
blocks.directed: What’s the offering?

blocks.text: The limited structures of embodiment.
blocks.directed: The limited structures of embodiment.

blocks.text: What’s the fire?
blocks.directed: What’s the fire?

blocks.text: Consciousness.
blocks.directed: Consciousness.

blocks.text: And who’s the divine recipient?
blocks.directed: And who’s the divine recipient?

blocks.text: Śiva.
blocks.directed: Śiva.

blocks.text: So the entire sacrificial process is ultimately an expression of the same reality.
blocks.directed: So the entire sacrificial process is ultimately an expression of the same reality.

blocks.text: The priest is Śiva’s power.
blocks.directed: The priest is Śiva’s power.

blocks.text: The fire is Śiva.
blocks.directed: The fire is Śiva.

blocks.text: The offering belongs to Śiva.
blocks.directed: The offering belongs to Śiva.

blocks.text: And the sacrifice discloses the nondual nature of the whole performance.
blocks.directed: And the sacrifice discloses the nondual nature of the whole performance.

blocks.text: It’s rather like turning up to a wedding and discovering you’re the bride, groom, priest, venue, and the entire congregation.
blocks.directed: It’s rather like turning up to a wedding and discovering you’re the bride, groom, priest, venue, and the entire congregation.

blocks.text: Except this is an internal metaphysical ritual rather than an unusually complicated marital arrangement.
blocks.directed: Except this is an internal metaphysical ritual rather than an unusually complicated marital arrangement.

blocks.text: And this is especially beautiful when compared with the Bhagavadgītā’s vision of sacrificial action.
blocks.directed: And this is especially beautiful when compared with the Bhagavadgītā’s vision of sacrificial action.

blocks.text: Different traditions develop the idea in different ways, but the structural resemblance is unmistakable.
blocks.directed: Different traditions develop the idea in different ways, but the structural resemblance is unmistakable.

blocks.text: The apparent separation between the act, its instruments, its object, and the divine reality is overcome through knowledge.
blocks.directed: The apparent separation between the act, its instruments, its object, and the divine reality is overcome through knowledge.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explicitly cites both the Vijñānabhairava and Bhagavadgītā when explaining the sūtra. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explicitly cites both the Vijñānabhairava and Bhagavadgītā when explaining the sūtra. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: The offering is not a rejection of embodiment.
blocks.directed: The offering is not a rejection of embodiment.

blocks.text: It is the end of mistaking embodiment for your ultimate identity.
blocks.directed: It is the end of mistaking embodiment for your ultimate identity.

blocks.text: And now we arrive at one of my favourite statements in the entire text.
blocks.directed: And now we arrive at one of my favourite statements in the entire text.

blocks.text: Because having turned the body into a sacrificial offering, Vasugupta announces that knowledge is dinner.
blocks.directed: Because having turned the body into a sacrificial offering, Vasugupta announces that knowledge is dinner.
